problem: Embodied agent evaluation relies on manually annotated VQA/MCQ pairs (costly, inconsistent, static) or high-level task success, which hides 'false positive successes' (wrong magnitude perception, redundant trial-and-error, coincidental success) and never tests spatial cognition directly.
motivation: Spatial cognition is the foundation of embodied tasks like navigation and manipulation, yet no scalable, oracle-free, embodiment-aware way exists to test it. Metamorphic testing avoids the oracle problem by checking logical and physical consistency of agent outputs on real execution trajectories.
key_idea: Generate spatial-cognition test cases automatically from real agent trajectories and detect errors as violations of logic- and physics-based metamorphic relations encoded as Prolog rules, with no ground-truth labels.
insight: Current MLLM agents fail badly at spatial cognition (average SC 0.44-0.52 vs human 0.96), particularly on directional tasks and egocentric-allocentric transformation, which outcome-based metrics miss. Errors mostly arise when translating spatial relations between reference frames. In the SC4-a study, CoT barely helps (0.11 to 0.15) while cognitive-map prompting gives a large gain (0.45). Threshold sensitivity tables show errors are gross violations rather than marginal misses.
method: Spatiotemporal state collection: sample state combinations (sliding window for SC1, persistent-object-based for SC2-4) from real trajectories; YOLOv11 tracking with confidence >0.6, and boxes added to the prompt to reduce perception confounds
Six MRs: logical (transitivity, symmetry, contradiction) and physical (triangle inequality, size-depth consistency under a pinhole model with eps=0.1, object size-ratio consistency with delta=0.05)
Test case generation: fill prompt templates per (SC, MR) to produce the original query x and the transformed query x'=phi(x); 30,300 test cases in total
Prolog validation: agent answers become facts, MRs become Horn-clause rules in SWI-Prolog, and all instantiations are enumerated to record violations

SC score: Score(SC_i)=1-|violations|/|test cases| across a taxonomy of 8 capabilities (SC1 movement perception, SC2 spatial reasoning, SC3 perspective visualization, SC4 ego-allocentric transformation, each split into directional/magnitude)
Human calibration: five participants set the MR5/MR6 tolerances at about the 90th percentile of human error and provide the human baseline

setting.backbone: GPT-5, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4, Qwen-VL, InternVL3.5-8B, DeepSeek-VL2-small (all frozen; agents under test)
setting.training_data: none (evaluation framework; test cases generated from existing trajectories of EB-Navigation (60), EB-Manipulation (48), AerialVLN drone subset (50))
setting.observation: egocentric RGB frames with YOLO bounding boxes in the prompt
setting.action_space: structured text answers (directions, step distances, sizes/depths in meters) about spatial relations; not low-level control
setting.privileged: none (YOLO detections are used to build queries)

numbers_note: No navigation benchmark results; the paper reports Spatial Cognition scores and error counts on its own test set, mostly in figures (heatmap/radar), so only the text values are usable. Text reports: GPT-5 avg SC 0.52, InternVL3.5-8B and DeepSeek-VL2-small 0.47, all agents 0.44-0.52, human 0.96, total errors 90,422.
results: MetaSpace flags 90,422 spatial cognition errors across 6 agents on 30,300 test cases each; error rates range from 43.06% (GPT-5) to 54.29% (GPT-4o). Scores are 0.44-0.52 vs human 0.96, and directional SC is below 0.38. MetaSpace captures 91.5% (988/1080) of meaningful errors in the union of errors found by all methods, versus 27-38% for VQA benchmarks, with 99.1% precision.
limitations: Only simulated environments and three scenarios; sim-to-real gap untested and only RGB MLLM agents evaluated
MRs check internal consistency only, so consistently wrong answers are missed (about 8.5% of meaningful errors); MR5/MR6 use human-calibrated thresholds that cause the few false positives
Mitigation studied only for SC4-a with GPT-4o and prompt engineering, without fine-tuning or architecture changes
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
